_note: Neighborhood and landmark prose, one entry per location. Section 1 of the location page template in SITE_ARCHITECTURE.md is 'Hero. This room, this neighborhood.', and until now the only geography on a location page was the street address in the plate. A local page that never says where it is, in words, is asking a search engine to work it out from a postal code.
_rule: EVERY SENTENCE HERE TRACES TO CLIENT_FACTS.md OR locations.json. No distances beyond the two miles between Convoy and Mercury, which SITE_ARCHITECTURE.md already states. No drive times, no freeway exits, no transit lines, no cross streets, none of which anyone has confirmed. Where a room has no confirmed landmark, it gets its street and its neighborhood and nothing more, which is still more than it had.
_html: Bodies carry inline HTML and are rendered with `| safe`. They are hand written in this file and never from user input.
_links: The nearest-neighbour rule in SITE_ARCHITECTURE.md is per location and is NOT all six. Mercury links Convoy, Convoy links Mercury, and nobody else links a sibling. Crown Point carries the prominent /noodle-room/ link its brief requires. Maui links nothing in San Diego, per its brief: 'Do not cross-link Maui into the San Diego set.'

convoy.title: On Convoy Street.
body: The room sits on Convoy Street in Kearny Mesa, in San Diego's Pan-Asian district, and it has held its corner of it since 2001. Lot parking.
Tajima Ramen Mercury is two miles up the road, and it is the bigger room.

mercury.title: Kearny Mesa, on Mercury Street.
body: Mercury is the Kearny Mesa room, on Mercury Street, and it is the one with parking on site.

It is two miles from the original on Convoy Street. Two rooms, two miles apart, and not the same room twice: Convoy is communal tables and the expanded izakaya list, Mercury is the ninety-seat room with the full bar and the sushi programme.

east-village.title: Walking distance from Petco Park.
body: The room is on E Street in East Village, downtown, walking distance from Petco Park. Street parking, and paid lots nearby.
It opened in 2016, seats roughly sixty-four, and the interior was built by Paul Basile of BASILE Studio.

college-heights.title: El Cajon Boulevard, near SDSU.
body: The ramen bar is on El Cajon Boulevard in the College Area, near San Diego State. Street parking.
It opened in 2020 and it is the newest format in the house: one long counter, an open kitchen you watch from, and the largest beer program of the seven.

crown-point.title: Ingraham Street, Crown Point.
body: The room is on Ingraham Street in Crown Point, in a building that does two jobs. Out front it is a restaurant, with street parking. Behind it is the commissary, where the broth for every San Diego location is made each morning and driven out before service.
The noodles are made in the same building. That is the Noodle Room, and it is why this address matters to the other five.

plaza-bonita.title: Inside Westfield Plaza Bonita.
body: This one is inside Westfield Plaza Bonita in National City, so it runs mall parking and mall hours rather than its own.
It is the only Tajima in the South Bay. Quick serve, a focused list, and no alcohol.

maui.title: South Kihei Road, Kihei.
body: Our only room outside California, on South Kihei Road in Kihei.
It carries the full ramen menu, sushi rolls, and izakaya plates, with dishes of its own that the San Diego rooms do not run.
